claims.text: The proposed intervention is severe plastic deformation.
Severe plastic deformation will refine the alloy's grain structure.
Grain refinement can reduce post-exposure toughness degradation in high-entropy alloys.
Grain size and its distribution mediate the effect of the intervention.
Reduced grain size increases grain-boundary area.
Increased grain-boundary area impedes dislocation movement.
Impeded dislocation movement reduces toughness degradation after heating.
The treated alloy will retain toughness better after service-relevant heating than an untreated alloy with the original grain structure.
The initial material is an as-designed high-entropy alloy possessing its original strength–ductility combination.
The untreated comparison baseline has the alloy's original grain structure.
The proposed exposure-temperature boundary is 473–1223 K.
The proposed exposure-duration boundary is up to three days.
The stated loading boundary is uniaxial tensile testing.
Toughness will be measured using a Charpy impact test or fracture-toughness test.
Failure to obtain a significant improvement in toughness retention over the untreated baseline will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The loading boundary is specified as uniaxial tensile testing, whereas the decisive toughness measurements are Charpy impact or fracture-toughness tests. These are distinct loading and specimen configurations, so the stated loading boundary does not consistently describe the proposed falsification experiment.
